sources.title: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes: In the Beginning, 1540 to 1750
sources.note: Official community history, indexed original full text. Archaeological ancestry is cautiously phrased; no blanket identification of every Plains Village site.

sources.title: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes: People of the Grass House, 1750 to 1820
sources.note: Official history, directly readable. Seasonal farming, pumpkin mats, house construction and extended families.

sources.title: Casana, Laugier, Hill and Blakeslee: A Council Circle at Etzanoa? (2020)
sources.note: American Antiquity 85, pp. 761 to 780, DOI 10.1017/aaq.2020.49. Publisher abstract and indexed NSF primary PDF https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10209663 checked. Etzanoa identification and council-circle function remain interpretations.

sources.title: Wichita State University: Anthropology student makes a big discovery (2017)
sources.note: June 7, 2017 institutional report, directly readable. June 5 find at 87 centimeters. Excludes unsupported generalizations about Indigenous iron use; traded status is Blakeslee’s interpretation.

sources.title: Chad Williams, Oklahoma Historical Society: Twin Villages, Battle of
sources.note: Institutional encyclopedia full indexed text: 1759 campaign, fortifications and Spanish withdrawal. Avoids uncertain casualty numbers.

sources.title: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes: Days of Darkness, 1820 to 1934
sources.note: Direct original, paragraphs on Camp Holmes, Civil War flight, schools and allotment. Exact land-opening year is avoided because page compresses allotment and opening chronology.

sources.title: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes: A New Beginning, 1934 to Present
sources.note: Official history, full indexed original. Modern government, family relationships and continuity.

sources.title: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes: Wichita-Pawnee Visitation
sources.note: Official community account, indexed original. Hosting, gifts, meals and cleaning the camp; no song quoted or fixed duration generalized.

sources.title: Bethke, Trabert and McAdams: Anchoring Sovereignty in Space (2024)
sources.note: American Antiquity 89, pp. 360 to 377, DOI 10.1017/aaq.2024.23. Indexed primary article introduction and direct abstract; ichaskhah camp on Camp Creek, used from the 1930s into the early 1960s. Coauthor Gary McAdams is affiliated with Wichita and Affiliated Tribes.

sources.title: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes: Language Class Dictionary
sources.note: Direct original, Simple Everyday Phrases entry: so:ti:cʔa / Thank you. Modern pedagogical transcription, not an early inscription.

sources.title: Meskwaki Nation: History
sources.note: Official history, directly readable and indexed. French Fox label, distinct Sauk alliance, 1845 removal and July 13, 1857 first 80-acre purchase. Excludes internally inconsistent acreage arithmetic.

sources.title: University of Iowa Office of the State Archaeologist: Meskwaki Culture and History
sources.note: Meskwaki Culture and History section, indexed original; migration and French conflicts. Related educator PDF https://history.iowa.gov/media/242/download?inline= printed p. 23.

sources.title: Lenville J. Stelle: History and Archaeology, Evidence of the 1730 Meskwaki Fortification
sources.note: Parkland College primary report, 1992, updated 2010. Direct original and indexed summary checked. Identification of site 11ML6 is argued, not certain; French-made artifacts alone do not identify French combatants.

sources.title: Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art: Frank Pushetonequa, Ribbon Appliqué Skirt
sources.note: Original collection record indexed in full via query "Ribbon Appliqué Skirt" "Meskwaki"; direct opening failed. Purchase from artist 1982 to 1983 is not an exact manufacture date. Accession 2025.56.38.

sources.title: Iowa State University Museums: The Meskwaki of Iowa
sources.note: Indexed original exhibition labels via query "The Meskwaki of Iowa" "Blouse"; direct opening failed. Cradleboard used by John Young Bear for Co-Ques-Se-We; its date is not borrowed from the separate circa-1920s blouse label.

sources.title: Meskwaki Nation: Annual Powwow
sources.note: Original indexed page, Origins of the Powwow section on corn storage, seasonal villages and celebrations. Stale upcoming-event dates not used.

sources.title: Meskwaki Annual Powwow: Powwow Origins
sources.note: Organizers’ indexed original history. Field Days 1902 to 1912 and first annual powwow 1913. Does not assert the event still occupies an unchanged site.

sources.title: Iowa PBS: Meskwaki Settlement School
sources.note: Direct original educational history. 1896 industrial day school and 1898 boarding school established without tribal leaders’ support.

sources.title: Meskwaki Nation Times: Romeo Buffalo’s 2021 graduation speech
sources.note: Volume 18 issue 06a, printed p. 12. Direct PDF access failed; exact indexed original reproduced with site:meskwaki.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Special-Graduation-Edition-2021final.pdf "Kemiskawisibeni". Speech by Namabyewa, Romeo Buffalo. Source explicitly supplies translated meaning rather than literal word-for-word English.

sources.title: Meskwaki Nation Times: July 2022, Red Earth Gardens
sources.note: Indexed original, printed p. 9, weekly Diabetes Share Program produce and last-Wednesday cooking demonstrations open to everyone. Planned farm facilities are not described as completed.

sources.title: Meskwaki Nation: Red Earth Gardens
sources.note: Official indexed program account, food sovereignty initiative begun in 2013, teaching and youth opportunities.

sources.title: Meskwaki Nation: Corn Harvest
sources.note: Official indexed 2025 report, students during language period harvesting Tama Flint corn with adults’ guidance at East Farm.

sources.title: Johnathan Buffalo, Meskwaki Nation: Museum Repatriation from Missouri State Museum
sources.note: Official Historic Preservation Director’s account, April 28, 2026, return of more than 200 Mary Alicia Owen collection objects after work begun in 1993. Incorrect expanded legal acronyms in the source are excluded.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Single historical Wichita record; no modern composite alias added.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: 1492 to 1783 index; decoded world1492 polygon bbox [-99.8920,31.3844,-95.0392,38.6161], broad southern Plains. Imported outline is not a bounded unified state.
batchIdentityNotes.limitations: Narrative distinguishes ancestral villages, eighteenth-century lifeways and specific modern Wichita and Affiliated Tribes. Does not absorb Wichita-Caddo-Delaware composite records.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Recommend sharing as phased records of the Meskwaki people; preserve both imported date ranges and outlines.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: fox index 1530 to 1783; decoded world1530 polygon bbox [-90.7047,44.0515,-87.9255,45.3325], Wisconsin. meskwahki-asa-hina-fox index 1492 to 1500, world1492 bbox [-85.2327,41.5884,-82.9034,42.4387], southern Michigan.
batchIdentityNotes.limitations: Public opening identifies approximate geographic phases rather than verified migration boundaries. Modern evidence focuses on Meskwaki Nation, Sac and Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa; no absorption of Sauk or of distinct Kansas/Nebraska and Oklahoma governments.
